title: Add tests for Prepare's idempotent fast path and git error paths
body:
## Problem

`internal/worktree/worktree_test.go` contains a single test, `TestPrepareCommitPushRoundTrip` (worktree_test.go:51), which only exercises the full happy path: clone → checkout → commit → push → verify remote branch. It never:

1. Calls `Prepare` a second time on the same `(owner, repo, issue)` to verify the existing-worktree short-circuit at `internal/worktree/worktree.go:77-79`:
   ```go
   // Already prepared (daemon cloned before container acquire).
   if st, statErr := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, ".git")); statErr == nil && st.IsDir() {
       return dir, branch, nil
   }
   ```
2. Exercises any git-command failure propagation paths in `git()`, `CommitAll`, `Push`, `ChangedLines`, or `Diff` — e.g. a bad clone URL, an invalid base branch name, or a rejected push.

## Why it matters

The "already prepared" short-circuit is a fragile, filesystem-presence-based idempotency check (it only verifies `.git` exists as a directory, not that the worktree is on the correct branch or otherwise valid). Since it is currently unverified by any test, a regression here (e.g. returning a stale/wrong branch, or failing to detect a corrupt partial clone) would go unnoticed. Similarly, all error-return branches in the git-wrapping methods are untested, so failures in argument construction or error wrapping (`fmt.Errorf("git %s: %w\n%s", ...)`) could silently break without any test catching it.

## Suggested fix

- Add a case to `TestPrepareCommitPushRoundTrip` (or a new test) that calls `m.Prepare` twice with the same arguments and asserts the second call returns the same `dir`/`branch` without re-cloning (e.g. assert no network/clone call occurs, or that repo state is unchanged).
- Add table-driven or dedicated tests for failure paths:
  - `Prepare` with a nonexistent base branch or bad clone URL, expecting a non-nil error.
  - `Push` against a URL/remote that rejects the push.
  - `CommitAll`, `ChangedLines`, `Diff` invoked in a directory that is not a valid git repo, expecting errors to propagate correctly.
